1.explanation:
• lib/features/copy-paste/BpmnCopyPaste.js: This module drives the copy→paste cycle, including the special logic that detects copying an Intermediate Event onto a Task and transforming it into a Boundary Event. It recreates a new businessObject for the Boundary Event but does not carry over the original extensionElements (async/job configuration).

• lib/features/copy-paste/ModdleCopy.js: Responsible for deep‐cloning BPMN/Moddle business objects. Any mis‐handling or filtering here (especially when the target type changes) will drop extensionElements. It’s used by BpmnCopyPaste to clone the source, but the resulting clone is never fully re‐applied when creating the new Boundary Event.

• lib/features/modeling/behavior/CreateBoundaryEventBehavior.js: Implements the shape creation logic when you drop/attach an event to a Task. When copying, this behavior is invoked to actually build the new boundary event shape. It constructs a fresh businessObject (via BpmnFactory) without copying across the Camunda extensions from the source.

• lib/features/modeling/behavior/AttachEventBehavior.js: Handles the attaching of events to host elements (Tasks). During copy→paste, this behavior finalizes the attachment but does not merge in extensionElements from the original event, resulting in a plain default Boundary Event.

• lib/features/modeling/behavior/BoundaryEventBehavior.js: Applies default BPMN semantics to Boundary Events (e.g. cancelActivity). By resetting properties to their defaults on new Boundary Events, any cloned extensions are potentially overwritten or never applied.
1.bug_scenario: When you copy an Intermediate Event that has Camunda-specific extensions configured (e.g. Async Continuations, Job Configuration) and then paste it onto a Task (causing it to be created as a Boundary Event), none of the previously filled extension‐based properties survive. The pasted Boundary Event ends up with only the default BPMN properties, losing all of the Camunda extensionElements that were present on the original Intermediate Event.

2.explanation:
1. lib/features/copy-paste/BpmnCopyPaste.js
   • This file contains the high-level logic for pasting elements, including special handling when you paste onto a target shape (like converting an Intermediate Event into a Boundary Event).
   • It orchestrates ModdleCopy to clone the businessObject, but then dispatches to modeling.create for the converted shape — in the conversion path the extensionElements aren’t re-applied.

2. lib/features/copy-paste/ModdleCopy.js
   • Responsible for deep-copying the BPMN businessObject, including extensionElements that hold custom Camunda properties.
   • The fact that these properties are copied correctly when pasting normally but dropped for boundary events points at a misuse or omission of ModdleCopy in the special paste path.

3. lib/features/modeling/behavior/CreateBoundaryEventBehavior.js
   • Implements the behavior when creating a Boundary Event (including via paste). It invokes the element factory to create a fresh businessObject of type BoundaryEvent, but doesn’t merge or re-apply the copied extensionElements from the original.
   • As a result, any Camunda extension properties on the original Intermediate Event are lost.

4. lib/features/modeling/behavior/AttachEventBehavior.js
   • Handles the attachment of events (including Boundary Events) to host elements, setting up DI shapes and wires, but it also does not reconcile extensionElements or custom Camunda attributes.
   • Since boundary event creation plus attachment is a two-step process, both behaviors need to participate in preserving properties; AttachEventBehavior never restores them after CreateBoundaryEventBehavior runs.
2.bug_scenario: When you copy an Intermediate Catch Event that has custom Camunda properties (e.g. async continuation, job priority, candidate starters, etc.) and then paste it onto a Task so that it becomes a Boundary Event, the pasted Boundary Event ends up with none of the previously configured properties. In other words, properties are preserved when you paste an Intermediate Event onto the diagram, but they are dropped when you paste it as a Boundary Event on a Task.
